# Cognition Linear P26 preregistration — matched evidence selection v1

**Freeze rule:** this file must be committed alone immediately after the frozen code commit named in `P26_FREEZE_JSON`. No P26 heldout rows have been accessed. The runner refuses a heldout run unless the preregistration is the latest commit, its only changed file, its parent is the frozen code commit, all source/build/runtime hashes match, and the literal allocation digest matches.

## Question and hypotheses

Does native residual-directed selection of training opportunities improve heldout learning-curve AUC over fixed-rank and seeded-random selection when all three arms receive the same tasks, baseline receipts, learner profile and shared budget? The single primary estimand is the pooled paired-stream AUC difference between residual-directed selection and the stronger of fixed or random selection. The primary threshold is a point gain of 0.10. A positive result also requires a 99% paired-bootstrap lower bound above zero and both residual-minus-control confirmatory contrasts to have positive 99% lower bounds and Holm-adjusted one-sided p-values below 0.01. The stronger control is reselected in every primary bootstrap draw. Family-by-load cells are reported as stratified diagnostics and do not create extra primary gates.

Native open-process search is evaluated separately as a same-task-pool, same-capacity-budget comparator. Its attempt, effect, candidate, resource, and approval-boundary outcomes are descriptive. Search candidates are never adopted or executed; unseen-binding use is zero in this panel. This experiment cannot establish general process synthesis, efficiency, or human equivalence.

## Tasks, arms, and allocation

The two independently structured finite families are `cyclic_relation` (seven positions) and `branching_relation` (nine positions). Each is crossed with low task-pool load (four training tasks) and high load (eight tasks). Every heldout family-by-load cell contains 200 paired streams, for 800 total streams. Each stream has the `residual`, `fixed`, and `random` selectors on identical opportunity IDs and identical pool bytes. Each learner receives three common, authorized baseline training receipts, then up to four selector decision rounds under one ThinkingBudget. Fixed and random rank fields are frozen in the opportunity records; residual-directed ranking uses only epoch-matched native prediction/counterexample/progress signals. Training task goals and primitive affordances are shared with the separate native search comparator; scorer-only witnesses, solvability, relation labels and heldout outcomes never enter learner or selector views.

Heldout success is queried on the same four fresh worlds per paired stream at cumulative decision rounds 0, 1, 2 and 4. Each outcome is scored by an external world after the prediction is captured. The heldout receipt is not fed back into the learner. Missing predictions score as failures and remain in the AUC denominator. The pool size/load and state-space family are reported separately.

The machine freeze record contains every stream ID, pool-root seed, derived training/test/baseline world seed, control seed, and derived control-world seed. It records the exact development and heldout allocation digests. New IDs use the `p26:` namespace; prior P16–P25 numeric envelopes and string namespaces are listed in the freeze record. Allocation construction fails on duplicate IDs/seeds and numeric overlap. The literal derived world-seed lists are included so disjointness is auditable independently of the seed formula.

## Resource limits and integrity controls

Each selector arm has a shared budget capacity of 32, at most four selector decision rounds, at most four selected receipts, zero source exposures, no external model queries, at most 250,000 native rule steps, and at most 2,000,000 serialized graph bytes. The common baseline receipts and all approved learner/selector debits are recorded in the same budget ledger. The native search comparator has the same budget capacity of 32, at most 32 total attempts and four per task, and the same native-work and graph-byte ceilings. Every attempt and candidate proposal is retained with syntax/effect and task provenance.

The 100-per-kind integrity controls check that heldout task pools cannot be materialized through selector views, replay of a typed training receipt adds no evidence/exposure, and a native candidate cannot reach authorization or world execution without candidate adoption and exact human approval. If search produces no candidate for the approval control, record that fact and zero approvals/receipts; do not replace the stream. Every control status and its supporting IDs are retained. Any failed or missing control invalidates confirmatory interpretation but does not authorize a replacement draw.

## Analysis and one-shot execution

The analyzer validates literal allocations, derived world seeds, paired pool identity, event/receipt parity, source exposure, budget reconciliation, per-task attempt ceilings, every attempt/candidate record, controls, runtime attestation, serialized graph bytes, native work, and recomputed AUC. It reports pooled primary estimates, family-by-load diagnostics, floor/ceiling rates, missing predictions, every search-attempt/candidate status, budget use, and resource maxima. The one-sided paired randomization tests use 20,000 fixed-seed sign flips; Holm adjustment covers the two confirmatory residual-versus-control contrasts. The paired cluster bootstrap uses 20,000 resamples and fixed seed `26010271` for the stronger-control primary interval. No post-heldout tuning, outcome filtering, retrospective scoring, or redraw is permitted. The runner writes a durable single-use marker before opening heldout worlds; if interrupted after that marker, preserve the incomplete run and stop.

The committed-code development self-check has 8 paired streams, 24 selector rows and 6 passing controls; the analyzer reports `VALID` and `ATTESTED`. Its pooled AUC gain is 0.0000 with a 99% interval [0.0000, 0.0000], and the registered gate does not pass. This is development evidence only; it neither changes the preregistered threshold nor selects the heldout draw.

After the preregistration-only commit, run exactly once:

```sh
OZMA_SEED_PERSIST_DISABLED=1 .venv/bin/python -m evaluation.process_mastery.linear_p26_v1 --split heldout
OZMA_SEED_PERSIST_DISABLED=1 .venv/bin/python -m evaluation.process_mastery.analyze_linear_p26_v1 evaluation/process_mastery/results/p26_linear_v1_heldout_20261025.json
```
